chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Getting known among Los Angeles musicians as a teenager
summary: Howard says he just took his horn and went to where the music was, having mastered alto and tenor in Ohio.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Well, when you'd been so busy playing music so much back in Ohio, and when you got here, when you had your horn you must have wanted to get into playing here like you were there, didn't you?

I did. You know, I wanted to get into Columbus, Ohio (inaudible) -- a team of people working there, I can't think of their names. It's gone, dear, I'm sorry. It's been a long time. But I -- I played by myself in Ohio, and my brother, oh, and my brother was playing drums and I was playing saxophone. And this was in Ohio.
Uh-huh.
Steubenville, Ohio.
Uh-huh.
And we played all the dances for the nights, you know, certain nights, and like that.
Would you hold your mike up?
I can't remember a name. I'm sorry.
That's okay. But I know -- you told us that you played with your brother and you played with a band, a large brass band, and you played in a school band, and then when you came out here --
I played in a school band, too.
Yeah. That was back in Ohio.
In Ohio.
But when you came out here how did you get -- your uncle and aunt already lived here, right?
Yeah, they were born here.
But they weren't involved in the music business in any way?
No.
So how did you manage -- how did you happen to get acquainted with the people in music here in Los Angeles? Was it -- I know you said you played in church here. Was it --
I played in church.
And how did you get acquainted with the other musicians in Los Angeles?
In Los Angeles? How did I get acquainted with them? Well, there wasn't no acquainting to get. You'd just take your horn and go down and play, that's all.
Oh, you'd just find out where the music was and go down to it.
Go down to it, yeah. That's all. And I loved to play.
I'm sure you must have because you'd been playing so much. So young.
I loved to play. I loved to play. And I love to play yet, too. Nobody don't pay any attention to me now.
Well, I don't know why they wouldn't.

Well me, I don't know why. Worst thing of it is I've got to fooling around with too many people, too much. But I want to thank you for -- please let me thank you for bringing that part out in me, please, because I was in Steubenville, Ohio, and I was born and raised there, and I come up as a little kid, and I had a horn, oh, and another thing, I was playing alto too, alto sax instead of soprano -- not soprano, instead of tenor. Alto.
You were playing alto when you came here?
Yeah.
So you'd already mastered two saxophones.
Huh?
You'd already mastered two saxophones by the time you got here as a teenager, both alto and tenor.
Yeh. I was playing two.
That's great. So you would find out where the music was in Los Angeles and go to it and then sit in with the musicians?
Yeah.
Where would you go to find it? I mean where was the music taking place? Was it jam sessions?
